STAGE: scope-and-evidence triage of the three proposals before scoring.
GOAL: decide for each proposal whether the behaviour signal, the curved operation, their single-pathway coupling, the switch set and the testable effect are all present, and which bundle evidence ids actually ground the behavioural claim.
READ: the three proposal texts (SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ, cocond-markov-poincare-ot, CURVCELL-SID) and the three frozen bundles 404ea254563870a6, bc19762831440f87, e9e97242e0e9ed08, rubric rubric-2026-10-v1. All three bundles share E5 (successor-entropy quintiles, top-1 mass 0.4375 down to 0.0543, mean distinct successors 2.7 to 41.4), E6/E7 (width-20 beam survival and teacher-forced NLL), E8 (first-level sharing 0.3106 at K=16 vs 0.0822 at K=256), E9 (cohort-profile 0.9291 vs 0.8871, strict overlap 0.5898), E10 (118315 edges, edge_density 5.33), E11 (same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067), E12/E13 (the proposed curved operation).
OBSERVED: all three name a training-only behaviour statistic (E1-E3) and an explicit curved operation in the quantizer (E12/E13), so none is out of scope on the four scope tests; the weaknesses are quality, not scope. SUCCFAN's lambda is a scalar function of ||x|| only. cocond defers alpha and q to an absent SAFEGUARDS section and has a column-rescaling step just before the argmax. CURVCELL's per-code s enlarges the cell of the high-branching code, i.e. the sign runs against its own motivation.
REASONING: E5 plus E10/E11 ground the behaviour dimension at 4 for SUCCFAN and cocond (measured statistic with support and coverage); CURVCELL gets 3 because the per-cell B[l][k] that actually drives it is not measured in the bundle, only per-item entropy is, and E8 points toward coarse cells rather than per-code curvature.
STILL OPEN: whether the geometry in each proposal is more than a matched Euclidean transform; handled in the per-proposal records.

STAGE: answer block for SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ.
GOAL: score the per-prefix conformal-factor proposal and test whether its "curvature" survives a matched Euclidean control.
READ: proposal SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ; bundle 404ea254563870a6 (E1-E3 signal, E5 fanout quintiles, E6/E7 beam survival and NLL, E8 first-level capacity, E10/E11 transition and prefix stats, E12/E13 conformal factor with c_p in (0.1,10)).
OBSERVED: lambda_p(x)=2/(1-c_p||x||^2) depends only on the radius, so on any prefix it is one positive scalar; encode r -> lambda r, decode c/lambda. Algebra: ||lambda r - c|| = lambda ||r - c/lambda||, so the assignment is exactly a Euclidean nearest-code search against the rescaled codebook C/lambda and the reconstruction loss is a 1/lambda^2 per-prefix weight. Also the stated geometry-off "c->0" limit is 2, not 1, so the "Euclidean" arm is a global 2x gain unless lambda=1 is set explicitly; and no clamp is given for 1-c_p||x||^2, which can go negative for c_p up to 10.
REASONING: behaviour 4 (E5 measured with coverage, E10/E11 support; E8 tension on the finer-resolution direction), geometry 2 (exact Euclidean per-node scalar-gain reproduction), novelty 3, downstream 3, falsifiability 3 (three arms exist but the c->0 arm is mis-specified), implementability 3 (cheap but unguarded denominator), exploration 3.
STILL OPEN: whether c_p is near-constant after normalisation (proposal's own risk); bounded check would be the variance of c_p over the 256 level-1 prefixes after the first assignment pass.

STAGE: answer block for cocond-markov-poincare-ot.
GOAL: score the Markov-diffused Poincare-cost Sinkhorn assignment and test whether the plan is driven by the cost or by the usage prior.
READ: proposal cocond-markov-poincare-ot; bundle bc19762831440f87 (E1-E3 popularity-adjusted transitions, E5 stratification, E8/E9 cohort and capacity evidence, E10 edge density 5.33, E11 prefix rate 0.0907 vs 0.067, E12/E13 Poincare cost and Einstein barycenter).
OBSERVED: the core equations are given, but alpha (diffusion strength) and q (column marginal) are deferred to a "SAFEGUARDS" section that is not in the bundle; the final iteration before argmax is P <- P*(q/colsum), a per-code rescaling. Minimal counterexample: equal costs, q=(0.9,0.1), comparable pre-scale columns -> code 1 is multiplied by 9x, so argmax picks it for every cost gap below log 9 regardless of curvature. Cost line also assumes sparse B_bt; a dense 1024x1024 B_bt is ~0.27 GFLOP per product, ~2.4 GFLOP per step, not the stated 5-8 MFLOPs.
REASONING: behaviour 4 (E5/E9/E11, consistent with E8), geometry 3 (genuine non-Euclidean cost but no matched Euclidean control argued), novelty 4 (moves the assignment plan itself), downstream 4 (specific plan-to-prefix chain with named observables and directions), falsifiability 4 (three arms, failure criterion, explicit "a rises / c flat" falsifier, but the Euclidean arm is only named), implementability 2 (alpha and q undefined under a no-tuning policy, cost estimate inconsistent), exploration 4.
STILL OPEN: whether B_bt is close to identity at edge density 5.33; bounded check is the mean row max of B_bt against 1/|batch|.

STAGE: answer block for CURVCELL-SID.
GOAL: score the per-code curvature-field proposal and test the direction and scale of its cell-size formula.
READ: proposal CURVCELL-SID; bundle e9e97242e0e9ed08 (E1-E3 per-cell branching B[l][k], E5 fanout bins, E8 first-level sharing, E10/E11 transition and prefix stats, E12/E13 kappa[l][k]=(log(1+B)/((d-1)R))^2 and D=d_B/sqrt(kappa)).
OBSERVED: larger B -> larger s -> D=d_B/s divided by a larger number -> the code wins for more points, i.e. the high-branching code gets a larger cell. With d=32, R=1: B=1 -> s=0.0224, B=44 -> s=0.1228; a point at d_B=0.1 scores 4.47 against the rare code and 0.81 against the hub, so the hub cell is 5.5x larger. The motivation asks for finer separation under fan-out prefixes, so the sign is inverted relative to the stated goal. (d-1) is a free constant: d=2 vs d=32 multiplies every D by 31. The geometry-off limit kappa->0 sends D to infinity, so the Euclidean arm is undefined as written. atanh argument is not explicitly clamped.
